title: "Filed Under: MLS strikers"
output: html_notebook

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(rstatix)
library(scales)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

fu_table <- function(df, ...) {
  df %>%
    knitr::kable(...) %>%
    kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = "condensed",
      full_width        = FALSE,
      position          = "left",
      font_size         = 13
    ) %>%
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "#282828", background = "#ECECEC")
}

conf_colors <- c(East = "#007bc6", West = "#69279b")
```


## Data

American Soccer Analysis (ASA), public API v1.
Downloaded 2026-09-25. MLS 2025 regular season (22 February – 18 October 2025,
510 matches).

Query parameters:
- `season_name = 2025`, `stage_name = Regular Season`
- `/players/xgoals`, all shots and penalties only, not split by team
- `/players/xgoals`, split by team, used to assign each player a primary team
- `/players/goals-added`, not split by team

> American Soccer Analysis. *ASA API v1: MLS player xGoals and Goals Added,
> 2025 Regular Season.* https://app.americansocceranalysis.com/api/v1/.
> Accessed 25 September 2026.

`data-prep.R` keeps players whose most common position in 2025 was striker
(`ST`), winger (`W`), or attacking midfielder (`AM`), and adds conference from
the 2025 alignment (15 teams each).

Variables:
- `position` — ASA general position: most common position played over the season
- `team`, `conference` — team with the most minutes played, and its conference
- `n_teams` — number of MLS teams played for in 2025
- `minutes` — regular-season minutes played
- `shots`, `shots_on_target`, `goals` — all shots, including penalties
- `xg` — expected goals: summed probability that each shot scores, from ASA's shot model
- `pen_shots`, `pen_goals`, `pen_xg` — the penalty subset of the above
- `key_passes`, `assists`, `xa` — passes leading to a shot, primary assists, and expected assists
- `g_plus` — ASA goals added (g+) above positional average, summed over all action types

```{r load}
raw <- readr::read_csv("data/mls-attackers-2025.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Dataset: %d observations, %d variables\n", nrow(raw), ncol(raw)))
```

Derived measures. Non-penalty figures remove penalty kicks, which are taken by
whoever the team designates and carry a near-fixed xG of about 0.78.
Age is measured at the season opener.

```{r derive}
attackers <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    npg      = goals - pen_goals,
    npxg     = xg - pen_xg,
    np_shots = shots - pen_shots,
    n90      = minutes / 90,
    g90      = goals / n90,
    npg90    = npg / n90,
    npxg90   = npxg / n90,
    conv     = npg / np_shots,
    sot_pct  = shots_on_target / shots,
    age      = floor(as.numeric(as.Date("2025-02-22") - birth_date) / 365.25)
  )
```


## Completeness checks

Per-90 rates from a few hundred minutes are unstable. A striker who scores once
in 150 minutes has a rate of 0.60 per 90, the same as a 20-goal season.

```{r completeness}
attackers %>%
  filter(position == "ST") %>%
  mutate(band = cut(minutes, c(0, 450, 900, 1800, 2700, Inf),
                    labels = c("< 450", "450–899", "900–1,799", "1,800–2,699", "2,700+"),
                    right = FALSE)) %>%
  group_by(band) %>%
  summarise(strikers = n(), goals = sum(goals)) %>%
  mutate(share_of_goals = percent(goals / sum(goals), accuracy = 1)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Minutes", "Strikers", "Goals", "Share of striker goals"))
```

Threshold: 900 minutes (ten full matches, about 30% of a 3,060-minute season).
This is applied to every ranking and test below. Season-total top-ten lists are
unaffected by it, since no striker under 900 minutes reached the top ten.

```{r filter}
MIN_MINUTES <- 900

strikers <- attackers %>%
  filter(position == "ST", minutes >= MIN_MINUTES)

strikers %>%
  count(conference) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Conference", "Strikers, 900+ minutes"))
```

Qualifying strikers who played for more than one team in 2025 are counted once,
under the team where they played more minutes.

```{r multi-team}
strikers %>%
  filter(n_teams > 1) %>%
  select(player, team, conference, minutes) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Primary team", "Conference", "Minutes"))
```


## Who counts as a striker

ASA assigns each player the position they played most often. Several of the
league's leading scorers are classified as wingers or attacking midfielders.
They are excluded from the striker rankings but shown here for reference.

```{r non-strikers}
attackers %>%
  filter(position != "ST", minutes >= MIN_MINUTES, goals >= 13) %>%
  arrange(desc(goals)) %>%
  select(player, position, team, goals, npg) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "ASA position", "Team", "Goals", "Non-penalty goals"))
```


## Top ten strikers

Ranked by goals, with ties broken by assists and then by fewer minutes (the
MLS Golden Boot tiebreakers).

```{r top10-fn}
top_ten <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    arrange(desc(goals), desc(assists), minutes) %>%
    slice_head(n = 10) %>%
    mutate(rank = row_number()) %>%
    transmute(
      rank, player, team,
      minutes = comma(minutes),
      goals, npg,
      sot     = shots_on_target,
      xg      = round(xg, 1),
      npxg    = round(npxg, 1),
      g90     = number(g90, accuracy = 0.01),
      npxg90  = number(npxg90, accuracy = 0.01),
      assists
    )
}

top10_cols <- c("#", "Player", "Team", "Min", "G", "npG", "SoT",
                "xG", "npxG", "G/90", "npxG/90", "A")
```

### Overall

```{r top10-overall}
strikers %>% top_ten() %>% fu_table(col.names = top10_cols)
```

### Eastern Conference

```{r top10-east}
strikers %>% filter(conference == "East") %>% top_ten() %>% fu_table(col.names = top10_cols)
```

### Western Conference

```{r top10-west}
strikers %>% filter(conference == "West") %>% top_ten() %>% fu_table(col.names = top10_cols)
```

### Beyond scoring

Chance creation and total on-ball value for the overall top ten. g+ is ASA's
goals added above the positional average, summed across passing, receiving,
dribbling, shooting, interrupting, and fouling.

```{r top10-creation}
strikers %>%
  arrange(desc(goals), desc(assists), minutes) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  transmute(player, key_passes, assists,
            xa     = round(xa, 1),
            g_plus = round(g_plus, 1)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Key passes", "Assists", "xA", "g+"))
```

Eight of the overall top ten played in the East. The tables below check whether
that holds beyond the top ten.


## Statistical tests

### Measures

Eight per-player rates, all among the 55 qualifying strikers.

```{r stat-measures}
strikers <- strikers %>%
  mutate(np_shots90    = np_shots / n90,
         npxg_per_shot = npxg / np_shots,
         diff90        = npg90 - npxg90)

measure_labels <- c(
  g90           = "Goals per 90",
  npg90         = "Non-penalty goals per 90",
  npxg90        = "Non-penalty xG per 90",
  np_shots90    = "Non-penalty shots per 90",
  npxg_per_shot = "xG per shot",
  conv          = "Conversion (npG / np shots)",
  sot_pct       = "Shots on target %",
  diff90        = "npG minus npxG, per 90"
)

strikers_long <- strikers %>%
  select(player, team, conference, all_of(names(measure_labels))) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(measure_labels)), names_to = "measure") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = names(measure_labels)))
```

```{r normality-check}
strikers_long %>%
  group_by(measure, conference) %>%
  shapiro_test(value) %>%
  mutate(measure   = measure_labels[as.character(measure)],
         statistic = number(statistic, accuracy = 0.001),
         p         = number(p, accuracy = 0.001)) %>%
  select(measure, conference, statistic, p) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Measure", "Conference", "W", "p"))
```

Three East measures (npG/90, conversion, and npG minus npxG) depart from
normality, so rank-based tests are used throughout.


### East vs. West

Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test per measure, East (n = 28) vs. West
(n = 27). P-values adjusted with Benjamini–Hochberg across the eight measures.
Effect size r = Z / √n (0.1 small, 0.3 moderate, 0.5 large).

```{r wilcoxon}
conf_medians <- strikers_long %>%
  group_by(measure, conference) %>%
  summarise(median = median(value), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = conference, values_from = median)

conf_tests <- strikers_long %>%
  group_by(measure) %>%
  wilcox_test(value ~ conference) %>%
  adjust_pvalue(method = "BH") %>%
  add_significance(p.col = "p.adj")

conf_effects <- strikers_long %>%
  group_by(measure) %>%
  wilcox_effsize(value ~ conference) %>%
  select(measure, effsize, magnitude)

conf_results <- conf_medians %>%
  left_join(conf_tests, by = "measure") %>%
  left_join(conf_effects, by = "measure")

conf_results %>%
  mutate(measure = measure_labels[as.character(measure)],
         across(c(East, West), ~ number(.x, accuracy = 0.01)),
         across(c(p, p.adj), ~ pvalue(.x, accuracy = 0.001)),
         effsize = number(effsize, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  select(measure, East, West, statistic, p, p.adj, p.adj.signif, effsize, magnitude) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Measure", "East median", "West median", "W", "p",
                         "p.adj (BH)", "", "r", "Magnitude"))
```

No measure differs between conferences after correction (all p.adj ≥ 0.32),
and every effect size is small. The East's hold on the top ten is not matched
by a difference in the typical striker.


### Age and scoring rate

```{r age-test}
strikers %>%
  cor_test(age, npg90, method = "spearman") %>%
  mutate(p = number(p, accuracy = 0.001)) %>%
  select(var1, var2, cor, p) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Variable", "Variable", "Spearman rho", "p"))
```

```{r age-oldest}
strikers %>%
  arrange(desc(age)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  mutate(npg_rank = min_rank(desc(strikers$npg))[match(player, strikers$player)]) %>%
  select(player, team, age, npg, npg_rank) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Team", "Age", "npG", "npG rank (of 55)"))
```


### Players vs. their conference and the league

Two approaches, following earlier Filed Under posts.

**Descriptive: IQR outliers.** Values beyond 1.5× the interquartile range from
the quartiles are outliers; beyond 3× are extreme outliers (`rstatix`
defaults). Run league-wide and within each conference, for every measure.

```{r player-outliers}
outliers_league <- strikers_long %>%
  group_by(measure) %>%
  mutate(group_median = median(value)) %>%
  identify_outliers(value) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(scope = "League")

outliers_conf <- strikers_long %>%
  group_by(conference, measure) %>%
  mutate(group_median = median(value)) %>%
  identify_outliers(value) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(scope = paste(conference, "only"))

player_outliers <- bind_rows(outliers_league, outliers_conf) %>%
  mutate(direction = if_else(value > group_median, "High", "Low"))

player_outliers %>%
  arrange(measure, scope, desc(value)) %>%
  mutate(measure = measure_labels[as.character(measure)],
         value   = number(value, accuracy = 0.01),
         level   = if_else(is.extreme, "Extreme", "Outlier")) %>%
  select(measure, scope, player, team, value, direction, level) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Measure", "Compared with", "Player", "Team", "Value",
                         "Direction", "Level"))
```

**Inferential: Poisson rate tests.** For each striker, an exact two-sided
Poisson test of non-penalty goals over 90-minute units against a reference
rate: the pooled rate of all other qualifying strikers (league), and the pooled
rate of all other qualifying strikers in the same conference (conference). The
player is left out of his own reference so he is not compared partly with
himself. P-values adjusted with Benjamini–Hochberg across the 55 strikers,
separately for each comparison.

```{r player-poisson}
rate_tests <- strikers %>%
  mutate(league_rate = (sum(npg) - npg) / (sum(n90) - n90)) %>%
  mutate(conf_rate   = (sum(npg) - npg) / (sum(n90) - n90), .by = conference) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(p_league = poisson.test(npg, n90, r = league_rate)$p.value,
         p_conf   = poisson.test(npg, n90, r = conf_rate)$p.value) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(p_league_adj = p.adjust(p_league, method = "BH"),
         p_conf_adj   = p.adjust(p_conf,   method = "BH"))

rate_tests %>%
  arrange(p_league) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%
  mutate(across(c(npg90, league_rate, conf_rate), ~ number(.x, accuracy = 0.01)),
         n90 = number(n90, accuracy = 0.1),
         across(c(p_league, p_league_adj, p_conf, p_conf_adj), ~ pvalue(.x, accuracy = 0.001))) %>%
  select(player, conference, npg, n90, npg90, league_rate, p_league, p_league_adj,
         conf_rate, p_conf, p_conf_adj) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Conf.", "npG", "90s", "npG/90",
                         "League rate", "p", "p.adj (BH)",
                         "Conf. rate", "p", "p.adj (BH)"))

rate_tests %>%
  summarise(sig_league_high = sum(p_league_adj < 0.05 & npg90 > league_rate),
            sig_league_low  = sum(p_league_adj < 0.05 & npg90 < league_rate),
            sig_conf_high   = sum(p_conf_adj   < 0.05 & npg90 > conf_rate),
            sig_conf_low    = sum(p_conf_adj   < 0.05 & npg90 < conf_rate)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Above league", "Below league",
                         "Above conference", "Below conference"))
```

### Players vs. their own xG

Same exact Poisson test, with non-penalty goals against non-penalty xG. The
reference ratio is the qualifying-striker pool's npG / npxG (0.90), not 1, so
each striker is measured against how strikers as a group finished in 2025
rather than against a model the whole league ran below (see the note on xG
below).

```{r player-vs-xg}
pool_ratio <- sum(strikers$npg) / sum(strikers$npxg)

xg_tests <- strikers %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(p_xg = poisson.test(npg, npxg, r = pool_ratio)$p.value) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(p_xg_adj = p.adjust(p_xg, method = "BH"))

xg_tests %>%
  arrange(p_xg) %>%
  slice_head(n = 6) %>%
  mutate(ratio = number(npg / npxg, accuracy = 0.01),
         npxg  = number(npxg, accuracy = 0.1),
         across(c(p_xg, p_xg_adj), ~ pvalue(.x, accuracy = 0.001))) %>%
  select(player, team, npg, npxg, ratio, p_xg, p_xg_adj) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Team", "npG", "npxG", "npG / npxG", "p", "p.adj (BH)"))
```

Summary. One striker differs significantly from both the league and his
conference: Lionel Messi (league p.adj < 0.001; East p.adj < 0.001). Milan
Iloski is an extreme outlier within the East on npG/90 but played 1,240
minutes, and his rate test does not survive correction (league p.adj = 0.145).
No striker scored significantly below the league or conference rate. No
striker's non-penalty goals differ significantly from his own xG after
correction (lowest p.adj = 0.817).


### Players vs. their team context

Does any striker score more than his team's performance would predict? Two
definitions of team performance, fitted separately:

- **A. Teammates' chance creation**: non-penalty xG per game created by the
  rest of the team, with the striker's own npxG subtracted so he does not set
  his own baseline.
- **B. Team results**: team points per game.

For each, a negative binomial regression of non-penalty goals on the team
measure, with log(90-minute units) as an offset. Negative binomial rather than
Poisson because striker goal counts are overdispersed (Pearson dispersion
1.44 under Poisson for model A). Each striker's expected total comes from a
model fitted to the other strikers (leave-one-out), so an extreme player does
not shift his own baseline. The observed total is compared with that
expectation using a two-sided exact test under the fitted negative binomial,
BH-adjusted across strikers.

Strikers who played for two teams in 2025 (3 of 55) are excluded: their xG
cannot be separated from team totals by team in this dataset.

```{r team-context-data}
teams_2025 <- readr::read_csv("data/mls-teams-2025.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(team_npg  = goals_for - pen_goals_for,
         team_npxg = xg_for - pen_xg_for,
         ppg       = points / games)

team_ctx <- strikers %>%
  filter(n_teams == 1) %>%
  left_join(teams_2025 %>% select(team, games, team_npg, team_npxg, ppg), by = "team") %>%
  mutate(rest_npxg_pg = (team_npxg - npxg) / games,
         share_npg    = npg / team_npg)

stopifnot(!any(is.na(team_ctx$team_npxg)))

team_ctx %>%
  summarise(strikers = n(),
            across(c(rest_npxg_pg, ppg),
                   list(min = min, median = median, max = max))) %>%
  mutate(across(-strikers, ~ number(.x, accuracy = 0.01))) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Strikers", "Teammate npxG/game: min", "median", "max",
                         "Team points/game: min", "median", "max"))
```

```{r team-context-models}
nb_fit <- function(df, context) {
  f <- if (context == "A") npg ~ log(rest_npxg_pg) + offset(log(n90))
       else                npg ~ ppg + offset(log(n90))
  MASS::glm.nb(f, data = df)
}

tibble(context = c("A. Teammates' npxG per game (log)", "B. Team points per game"),
       fit     = list(nb_fit(team_ctx, "A"), nb_fit(team_ctx, "B"))) %>%
  mutate(coef = map(fit, ~ broom::tidy(.x) %>% filter(term != "(Intercept)")),
         theta = map_dbl(fit, "theta")) %>%
  unnest(coef) %>%
  transmute(context,
            rate_ratio = number(exp(estimate), accuracy = 0.01),
            estimate   = number(estimate, accuracy = 0.001),
            std.error = number(std.error, accuracy = 0.001),
            statistic = number(statistic, accuracy = 0.01),
            p.value   = pvalue(p.value, accuracy = 0.001),
            theta     = number(theta, accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  select(context, estimate, rate_ratio, std.error, statistic, p.value, theta) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Team context", "Coefficient", "Rate ratio", "SE", "z", "p", "θ"))
```

Rate ratio: the multiplier on a striker's expected scoring rate per one-unit
increase in the team measure (for A, per one-unit increase in log teammate
npxG, i.e. multiplying teammate npxG by e ≈ 2.7).

```{r team-context-tests}
nb_p <- function(x, mu, theta) {
  lower <- pnbinom(x, size = theta, mu = mu)
  upper <- pnbinom(x - 1, size = theta, mu = mu, lower.tail = FALSE)
  min(1, 2 * min(lower, upper))
}

loo_expected <- function(df, context) {
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    fit <- suppressWarnings(nb_fit(df[-i, ], context))
    tibble(expected = unname(predict(fit, newdata = df[i, ], type = "response")),
           theta    = fit$theta)
  })
}

context_tests <- map_dfr(c("A", "B"), function(ctx) {
  team_ctx %>%
    bind_cols(loo_expected(team_ctx, ctx)) %>%
    mutate(p = pmap_dbl(list(npg, expected, theta), nb_p),
           p.adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
           context = ctx)
})

context_tests %>%
  select(context, player, team, npg, expected, p, p.adj) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = context, values_from = c(expected, p, p.adj)) %>%
  arrange(p_A) %>%
  slice_head(n = 8) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("expected"), ~ number(.x, accuracy = 0.1)),
         across(matches("^p(\\.adj)?_"), ~ pvalue(.x, accuracy = 0.001))) %>%
  select(player, team, npg, expected_A, p_A, p.adj_A, expected_B, p_B, p.adj_B) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Team", "npG",
                         "Expected (A)", "p", "p.adj (BH)",
                         "Expected (B)", "p", "p.adj (BH)"))

context_tests %>%
  group_by(context) %>%
  summarise(above = sum(p.adj < 0.05 & npg > expected),
            below = sum(p.adj < 0.05 & npg < expected)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Team context", "Significantly above expected",
                         "Significantly below expected"))
```

Some leave-one-out fits reach the iteration limit when estimating θ. This
happens when the remaining data are close to Poisson (θ large), where the
negative binomial converges to the Poisson. The Poisson version of the same
tests identifies the same single striker (Messi; p.adj = 0.001 for A, 0.010
for B).

**Share of team goals.** Descriptive only: each striker's non-penalty goals as
a share of his team's non-penalty goals.

```{r team-share}
team_ctx %>%
  arrange(desc(share_npg)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%
  mutate(share_npg = percent(share_npg, accuracy = 1)) %>%
  select(player, team, npg, team_npg, share_npg) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Team", "npG", "Team npG", "Share"))
```


## The gap

Non-penalty goals, attacking players, 900+ minutes. No player at any other
position scored more than 9 non-penalty goals in 2025 (ASA, all positions,
same query), so this ranking holds league-wide.

```{r gap}
npg_rank <- attackers %>%
  filter(minutes >= MIN_MINUTES) %>%
  arrange(desc(npg)) %>%
  mutate(rank = min_rank(desc(npg)))

npg_rank %>%
  slice_head(n = 6) %>%
  select(rank, player, position, team, age, npg, goals) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("#", "Player", "Pos.", "Team", "Age", "npG", "G"))

first  <- npg_rank$npg[1]
second <- npg_rank$npg[2]
gap    <- first - second

# Every player within less than one gap of second place
below_second <- npg_rank %>% filter(npg > second - gap)
last_rank    <- nrow(below_second)
last_npg     <- min(below_second$npg)

striker_median_npg90 <- median(strikers$npg90)
messi_npg90 <- strikers %>% filter(player == "Lionel Messi") %>% pull(npg90)

cat(sprintf(paste0(
  "Ranks 1 to 2: %d to %d npG, %d apart.\n",
  "Ranks 2 to %d: %d to %d npG, %d apart.\n",
  "Messi npG/90: %.2f. Striker median npG/90: %.2f (%.1fx).\n"),
  first, second, gap,
  last_rank, second, last_npg, second - last_npg,
  messi_npg90, striker_median_npg90, messi_npg90 / striker_median_npg90))
```

Strikers only, as shown in the hero chart (top 15).

```{r gap-strikers}
striker_top15 <- strikers %>% slice_max(npg, n = 15, with_ties = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("Strikers, ranks 1 to 2: %d to %d npG. Ranks 2 to 15: %d to %d npG, %d apart.\n",
            striker_top15$npg[1], striker_top15$npg[2],
            striker_top15$npg[2], striker_top15$npg[15],
            striker_top15$npg[2] - striker_top15$npg[15]))
```


## A note on expected goals in 2025

Across every MLS player, 2025 produced 1,355 non-penalty goals from 1,519
non-penalty xG, a ratio of 0.89. For 2019 and 2021–2024 the same ratio was
0.94, 0.99, 1.03, 0.995, and 1.02 (ASA API, same query by season, retrieved
2026-09-25). Either scoring fell short of chance quality league-wide in 2025,
or the shot model's calibration shifted. The data does not distinguish between
the two. Goals-minus-xG comparisons in this notebook are therefore relative to
a league that ran 11% below its own model, and are not used for the published
finding.

```{r finishing}
strikers %>%
  summarise(strikers = n(), below_npxg = sum(npg < npxg),
            npg = sum(npg), npxg = sum(npxg)) %>%
  relocate(below_npxg, .after = npxg) %>%
  mutate(npxg = round(npxg), ratio = number(npg / npxg, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Strikers", "npG", "npxG", "Below own npxG", "npG / npxG"))
```


## Predictors of over- and underperformance

### Outcome

A player overperforms when non-penalty goals per 90 exceed non-penalty xG per
90 (ratio > 1), and underperforms when the ratio is below 1. Both rates share
the same denominator (90-minute units), so the ratio reduces to npG / npxG and
the outcome is equivalent to npG > npxG.

The pool is every striker, winger, and attacking midfielder with 900+ minutes.
Position enters as a predictor. Strikers alone are fitted as a sensitivity
check.

Because the league as a whole ran at 0.89 goals per non-penalty xG in 2025
(see the note above), a threshold of 1 classifies most players as
underperforming.

```{r enet-outcome}
model_pool <- attackers %>%
  filter(minutes >= MIN_MINUTES) %>%
  mutate(
    over          = as.integer(npg > npxg),
    west          = as.integer(conference == "West"),
    multi_team    = as.integer(n_teams > 1),
    np_shots90    = np_shots / n90,
    npxg_per_shot = npxg / np_shots,
    pen_shots90   = pen_shots / n90,
    key_passes90  = key_passes / n90,
    assists90     = assists / n90,
    xa90          = xa / n90,
    pos_W         = as.integer(position == "W"),
    pos_AM        = as.integer(position == "AM")
  )

model_pool %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  summarise(players = n(), under = sum(over == 0), over = sum(over)) %>%
  relocate(under, .after = over) %>%
  bind_rows(summarise(., position = "All", across(c(players, over, under), sum))) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Position", "Players", "Overperforming", "Underperforming"))
```

### Predictors

Every variable in the dataset that does not contain the outcome. Volume
measures are expressed per 90.

| Predictor | Definition |
|---|---|
| `age` | Age at the 2025 season opener |
| `minutes` | Regular-season minutes |
| `west` | Primary team in the Western Conference |
| `multi_team` | Played for more than one team |
| `np_shots90` | Non-penalty shots per 90 |
| `npxg_per_shot` | Average non-penalty xG per shot (shot quality) |
| `sot_pct` | Share of all shots on target |
| `pen_shots90` | Penalty attempts per 90 |
| `key_passes90`, `assists90`, `xa90` | Chance creation for teammates, per 90 |
| `pos_W`, `pos_AM` | Winger, attacking midfielder (reference: striker) |

Excluded because they contain the outcome: goals, npG, npG/90, npxG/90,
conversion rate (npG per non-penalty shot), and g+ (its shooting component
credits goals scored). `npxg90` is also the product of `np_shots90` and
`npxg_per_shot`, so it is represented by those two. Penalty goals and penalty
xG are left out as near-duplicates of penalty attempts. Team identity (30
levels for 153 players) is left out; conference stands in for it.

`sot_pct` is partly mechanical: every goal is a shot on target. Models are
reported with and without it.

```{r enet-predictors}
predictors_all <- c("age", "minutes", "west", "multi_team", "np_shots90",
                    "npxg_per_shot", "sot_pct", "pen_shots90",
                    "key_passes90", "assists90", "xa90", "pos_W", "pos_AM")

model_pool %>%
  select(all_of(predictors_all)) %>%
  cor() %>%
  as_tibble(rownames = "predictor") %>%
  pivot_longer(-predictor, names_to = "with", values_to = "r") %>%
  filter(predictor < with, abs(r) >= 0.5) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(r))) %>%
  mutate(r = number(r, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Predictor", "With", "Pearson r"))
```

The chance-creation measures are correlated with one another. The elastic net
mixing penalty is chosen for this reason: the ridge component shares weight
across correlated predictors, and the lasso component sets weak ones to zero.

### Model

Penalised logistic regression (`glmnet`), predictors standardised to mean 0 and
SD 1 so coefficients are comparable. The mixing parameter α is fixed at 0.5.
The penalty strength λ is chosen by 5-fold cross-validation.

Performance is measured by area under the ROC curve (AUC; 0.5 is chance),
estimated by nested cross-validation: λ is tuned inside each training fold and
AUC is scored only on the held-out fold, repeated 20 times. Cross-validated
AUC on shuffled labels sits below 0.5 in small samples, so each model is
compared with 100 permutations of the outcome rather than with 0.5.

```{r enet-functions}
library(glmnet)

ALPHA <- 0.5

standardise <- function(df, preds) {
  df %>% select(all_of(preds)) %>% mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)))) %>% as.matrix()
}

auc <- function(y, p) {
  r  <- rank(p)
  n1 <- sum(y)
  n0 <- length(y) - n1
  (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}

nested_auc <- function(X, y, reps = 20, seed = 1) {
  map_dbl(seq_len(reps), function(r) {
    set.seed(seed + r)
    outer <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(y)))
    p <- numeric(length(y))
    for (k in 1:5) {
      train <- outer != k
      cv <- cv.glmnet(X[train, ], y[train], family = "binomial", alpha = ALPHA, nfolds = 5)
      p[!train] <- predict(cv, X[!train, , drop = FALSE], s = "lambda.min", type = "response")
    }
    auc(y, p)
  }) %>% mean()
}

permutation_test <- function(X, y, B = 100) {
  observed <- nested_auc(X, y)
  null <- map_dbl(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    set.seed(1000 + b)
    nested_auc(X, sample(y), reps = 2, seed = b)
  })
  tibble(auc = observed, null_mean = mean(null),
         null_95 = unname(quantile(null, 0.95)),
         p = (1 + sum(null >= observed)) / (B + 1))
}
```

```{r enet-fit}
model_strikers <- model_pool %>% filter(position == "ST")
predictors_st  <- setdiff(predictors_all, c("pos_W", "pos_AM"))

configs <- tribble(
  ~pool,       ~predictors,                       ~data,
  "Attackers", "All",                             list(model_pool),
  "Attackers", "Without SoT%",                    list(model_pool),
  "Strikers",  "All",                             list(model_strikers),
  "Strikers",  "Without SoT%",                    list(model_strikers)
) %>%
  mutate(
    preds = list(predictors_all, setdiff(predictors_all, "sot_pct"),
                 predictors_st,  setdiff(predictors_st,  "sot_pct")),
    data  = map(data, 1)
  )

enet_results <- configs %>%
  mutate(
    n      = map_int(data, nrow),
    over   = map_int(data, ~ sum(.x$over)),
    result = map2(data, preds, ~ permutation_test(standardise(.x, .y), .x$over))
  ) %>%
  unnest(result)

enet_results %>%
  transmute(pool, predictors, n, over,
            auc       = number(auc, accuracy = 0.01),
            null_mean = number(null_mean, accuracy = 0.01),
            null_95   = number(null_95, accuracy = 0.01),
            p         = number(p, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Pool", "Predictors", "n", "Over", "Nested-CV AUC",
                         "Permuted AUC (mean)", "Permuted AUC (95th pct)", "Permutation p"))
```

### Which predictors

Coefficients at the cross-validated λ for the full attacker pool, and how often
each predictor is retained across 200 bootstrap resamples (λ re-tuned in
each). Coefficients are on the standardised scale: the change in log-odds of
overperforming per one-SD increase. A dot means the predictor was set to zero.

Selection at λ.min is permissive. Predictors with no relationship to the
outcome are still retained in roughly 40–55% of resamples here, so only
frequencies near 100% separate from that background.

```{r enet-bootstrap}
bootstrap_selection <- function(df, preds, B = 200) {
  X <- standardise(df, preds)
  y <- df$over
  map_dfr(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    set.seed(b)
    i  <- sample(nrow(X), replace = TRUE)
    cv <- cv.glmnet(X[i, ], y[i], family = "binomial", alpha = ALPHA, nfolds = 5)
    cf <- as.matrix(coef(cv, s = "lambda.min"))[-1, 1]
    tibble(predictor = names(cf), coef = cf)
  }) %>%
    group_by(predictor) %>%
    summarise(selected = mean(coef != 0),
              positive = mean(coef > 0),
              negative = mean(coef < 0))
}

full_coefs <- function(df, preds) {
  set.seed(1)
  cv <- cv.glmnet(standardise(df, preds), df$over, family = "binomial",
                  alpha = ALPHA, nfolds = 5)
  cf <- as.matrix(coef(cv, s = "lambda.min"))[-1, 1]
  tibble(predictor = names(cf), coef = cf)
}

selection <- bind_rows(
  full_coefs(model_pool, predictors_all) %>%
    left_join(bootstrap_selection(model_pool, predictors_all), by = "predictor") %>%
    mutate(model = "With SoT%"),
  full_coefs(model_pool, setdiff(predictors_all, "sot_pct")) %>%
    left_join(bootstrap_selection(model_pool, setdiff(predictors_all, "sot_pct")), by = "predictor") %>%
    mutate(model = "Without SoT%")
)

selection %>%
  select(predictor, model, coef, selected) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = c(coef, selected)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`selected_With SoT%`)) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("coef"), ~ if_else(.x == 0 | is.na(.x), "·", number(.x, accuracy = 0.001))),
         across(starts_with("selected"), ~ if_else(is.na(.x), "–", percent(.x, accuracy = 1)))) %>%
  select(predictor, `coef_With SoT%`, `selected_With SoT%`,
         `coef_Without SoT%`, `selected_Without SoT%`) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Predictor", "Coef. (with SoT%)", "Bootstrap selected",
                         "Coef. (without SoT%)", "Bootstrap selected"))
```

```{r enet-plot, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
selection %>%
  mutate(direction = if_else(positive >= negative, "Toward overperforming", "Toward underperforming"),
         predictor = fct_reorder(predictor, selected, .fun = max)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(selected, predictor, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~model, ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Toward overperforming` = "#007bc6",
                               `Toward underperforming` = "#69279b")) +
  labs(title = "Bootstrap selection frequency, elastic net (α = 0.5)",
       subtitle = "Attackers, 900+ minutes, 200 resamples. Color: sign of the coefficient",
       x = "Share of resamples retaining the predictor", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r enet-position-check}
model_pool %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  summarise(players = n(), npg = sum(npg), npxg = sum(npxg),
            key_passes90 = median(key_passes90)) %>%
  mutate(ratio = number(npg / npxg, accuracy = 0.01),
         npxg = round(npxg),
         key_passes90 = number(key_passes90, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  select(position, players, npg, npxg, ratio, key_passes90) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Position", "Players", "npG", "npxG", "npG / npxG", "Median key passes / 90"))
```

### Result

With shots-on-target rate included, the attacker model separates over- from
underperformers moderately (nested-CV AUC 0.70; permutation p = 0.01).
Shots-on-target rate carries most of that, and it is partly the outcome
restated: goals are a subset of shots on target.

Without it, performance drops to AUC 0.57 (p = 0.03). Two predictors are
retained in nearly every resample, both positive: playing as an attacking
midfielder, and key passes per 90. The two overlap. Attacking midfielders
make the most key passes, and as a group they scored 26% above their npxG in
2025 while strikers and wingers finished 10–13% below. In a season where the
league as a whole ran 11% below its model, the position effect cannot be
separated from how the xG model treats the shots attacking midfielders take.

Among strikers alone, no predictor set does better than shuffled labels once
shots-on-target rate is removed (AUC 0.36; p = 0.61). Age, conference, minutes,
shot volume, shot quality, penalty duty, and chance creation do not
distinguish strikers who beat their xG from strikers who did not.

### F. Funnel plot (hero)

Non-penalty goals per 90 against minutes played for all 55 qualifying strikers.
Control limits are exact Poisson 95% and 99.8% limits around the pooled striker
rate, smoothed between integer counts (Spiegelhalter 2005). The limits are not
adjusted for multiple comparisons; the BH-adjusted rate tests above are the
formal result.

```{r funnel-limits}
funnel_rate <- sum(strikers$npg) / sum(strikers$n90)

poisson_limit <- function(p, mu) {
  x <- qpois(p, mu)
  a <- (ppois(x, mu) - p) / dpois(x, mu)
  pmax(x - a, 0)
}

funnel <- tibble(n90 = seq(900, 3650, by = 5) / 90) %>%
  mutate(mu    = funnel_rate * n90,
         lo95  = poisson_limit(0.025, mu) / n90,
         hi95  = poisson_limit(0.975, mu) / n90,
         lo998 = poisson_limit(0.001, mu) / n90,
         hi998 = poisson_limit(0.999, mu) / n90)

funnel_strikers <- strikers %>%
  mutate(hi998 = poisson_limit(0.999, funnel_rate * n90) / n90,
         hi95  = poisson_limit(0.975, funnel_rate * n90) / n90,
         lo95  = poisson_limit(0.025, funnel_rate * n90) / n90,
         zone  = case_when(npg90 > hi998 ~ "Above 99.8%",
                           npg90 > hi95  ~ "Between 95% and 99.8%",
                           npg90 < lo95  ~ "Below 95%",
                           TRUE          ~ "Inside 95%"))

funnel_strikers %>%
  count(zone) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Zone", "Strikers"))

funnel_strikers %>%
  filter(zone != "Inside 95%") %>%
  arrange(desc(npg90)) %>%
  mutate(npg90 = number(npg90, accuracy = 0.01), minutes = comma(minutes)) %>%
  select(player, team, minutes, npg, npg90, zone) %>%
  fu_table(col.names = c("Player", "Team", "Minutes", "npG", "npG/90", "Zone"))
```

With 55 strikers, about 1.4 would fall above the 95% line by chance alone
(2.5% each side). Five do: four between the 95% and 99.8% lines, and one
above 99.8%. None falls below the lower 95% line.

```{r plot-funnel, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, ymin = lo998, ymax = hi998), fill = "#eef4f5") +
  geom_ribbon(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "#69279b", alpha = 0.14) +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, hi95), linetype = "dashed", color = "#676767") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, lo95), linetype = "dashed", color = "#676767") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, hi998), color = "#676767") +
  geom_line(data = funnel, aes(n90 * 90, lo998), color = "#676767") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = funnel_rate, color = "#676767") +
  geom_point(data = funnel_strikers, aes(minutes, npg90,
                                         fill = zone == "Above 99.8%"),
             shape = 21, color = "#282828", size = 2.4, stroke = 0.35) +
  geom_text_repel(data = filter(funnel_strikers, zone %in% c("Above 99.8%", "Between 95% and 99.8%")),
                  aes(minutes, npg90, label = player), size = 3, seed = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#007bc6", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(900, 3650), ylim = c(0, 1.08)) +
  labs(title = "Non-penalty goals per 90 by minutes played",
       subtitle = "Strikers, 900+ minutes. Bands: exact Poisson 95% and 99.8% limits",
       x = "Minutes played", y = "npG per 90") +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Finding

Of 55 MLS strikers with 900 or more regular-season minutes in 2025, one scored
non-penalty goals at a rate outside the range expected by chance: Lionel
Messi, 0.93 per 90 against a pooled rate of 0.37, beyond the 99.8% Poisson
limit for his minutes. Four others fell between the 95% and 99.8% limits;
none fell below. Messi's 28 non-penalty goals were nine more than any other
player at any position. He is the only striker whose rate differs
significantly from the league, from his own conference, and from what his
team's performance predicts. Eastern and Western Conference strikers do not
differ on any of eight measures.


## Observations

- On the funnel plot, one of 55 strikers falls above the 99.8% limit (Messi).
  Four fall between the 95% and 99.8% limits (Iloski, Musovski, Baribo,
  White); none falls below the lower 95% limit. About 1.4 would be expected
  above the upper 95% limit by chance.
- Lionel Messi scored 28 non-penalty goals (0.93 per 90). The next-highest
  total at any position was 19. His rate was significantly above the rest of
  the league (0.35 per 90; exact Poisson test, p.adj < 0.001) and the rest of
  the Eastern Conference (0.37 per 90; p.adj < 0.001). No other striker
  differed significantly from either reference.
- He was 37 at the season opener, the second-oldest of 55 qualifying strikers.
  Across those 55, age and non-penalty scoring rate were not related
  (Spearman rho = 0.12, p = 0.39).
- Eight of the ten top-scoring strikers played in the Eastern Conference. The
  full pools do not differ on any measure: goals per 90 (W = 480,
  p.adj = 0.320), non-penalty goals per 90 (W = 471, p.adj = 0.320),
  non-penalty shots per 90 (W = 494, p.adj = 0.320), or the five others (all
  p.adj ≥ 0.475). All effect sizes are small.
- Milan Iloski (Philadelphia) is an extreme outlier within the East on
  non-penalty goals per 90 (0.87) in 1,240 minutes. His rate test does not
  survive correction (p.adj = 0.145).
- No striker's non-penalty goal total differs significantly from his own xG
  after correction (lowest p.adj = 0.817, Iloski: 12 goals from 6.1 xG).
- Relative to team context, one striker scored significantly more than
  expected: Messi, 28 non-penalty goals against 11.0 expected from his
  teammates' chance creation (negative binomial, p.adj = 0.001) and 12.7
  expected from his team's points per game (p.adj = 0.015). No striker scored
  significantly below expectation under either definition.
- Team results were associated with striker scoring: each additional point
  per game was associated with a 1.61× higher non-penalty scoring rate
  (z = 3.23, p = 0.001). Teammates' chance creation was not (rate ratio 1.47
  per log unit, p = 0.177).
- Sam Surridge scored 39% of Nashville's non-penalty goals, the largest share
  of any striker's team total. Joveljic (36%, Kansas City) and Messi (35%,
  Miami) followed.
- Four of the top ten (Surridge, Joveljic, Choupo-Moting, A. Martínez) scored
  five penalties each. Messi scored one.
- Among qualifying strikers, no measured characteristic other than
  shots-on-target rate predicted whether a striker scored above or below
  expected (elastic net, nested-CV AUC 0.36 without it; permutation p = 0.61).
